quick.summary: How to use spacing to group related items, and where to place primary buttons.
quick.takeaway: Group items with invisible space, and anchor your primary actions at the end.

parts.title: Group related things

beats.line: Our settings page feels incredibly messy. Why does it look like a junk drawer?
Think of a road sign. It puts cities in one list, distances in another.
They group things by leaving space between them.
Space is invisible. How does it group anything?
Your brain connects items that sit near each other.
We call this the law of proximity.
Can I just say put related things together?
Yes. Grouping beats drawing actual lines.
Okay, so I group the profile fields. But what about the save buttons?

parts.cliff: Find out where to place the primary actions.

beats.line: Buttons are actions. They sit outside the groups.
I dropped them at the bottom. But they still get lost.
Put them where the eye finishes reading.
In English, we read across, then move down.
Like a printed page. The eye stops at the bottom right.
Exactly. We place primary actions at the end of that path.
So the save button anchors the bottom corner of the form.
Yes. It catches them right when they finish deciding.

board.text: save button at end of path

beats.line: I will bunch the inputs, and pin the button bottom right.
Your messy drawer is now a clear path.

quiz.question: Why do we leave empty space between groups of settings?
options: The brain naturally connects things that sit close together.
Space forces the user to read the text slower.
It prevents accidental clicks on smaller mobile screens.
Every layout needs enough white space to look modern.
quiz.explanation: Space is an invisible tool. We use it to group related items without drawing cluttered lines.

quiz.question: Primary actions like a save button should always go at the top of the form.
quiz.explanation: False. Place them at the end of the reading path, usually the bottom right corner.
